summary: Most Gmail read and modify scopes are restricted. Expect app verification, plus an annual security assessment if your servers store or transmit mail. Google says the restricted process can take several weeks.

verdict.label: Verification needed: weeks
verdict.effort: Several setup steps including a demo video; more if a security assessment applies. Effort not measured.
verdict.wait: Google says restricted scope verification can potentially take several weeks; branding verification typically takes 2-3 business days. No timeline is published for the security assessment.
verdict.reason: Public apps that use sensitive or restricted scopes must be verified. Reading or modifying mail uses restricted scopes, and apps that store or transmit restricted data on servers must complete a security assessment from a Google-approved assessor, repeated at least every 12 months. Unverified apps are capped at 100 users.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Open Google Cloud Console and create a project for your app.

steps.title: Set up branding and the OAuth consent screen
steps.detail: Enter your app name, logo, homepage and privacy policy link, and add an authorized domain you own. Verify ownership of every authorized domain in Google Search Console. Google's pages call this screen both the Branding page and the OAuth consent screen. Keep the project contact email current, because Google sends verification messages there.

steps.title: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.detail: gmail.labels is non-sensitive and gmail.send is sensitive. gmail.readonly, gmail.compose, gmail.insert, gmail.modify, gmail.metadata and https://mail.google.com/ are restricted. An agent can map your use case to the narrowest scope that works. Google also asks you to explain why narrower scopes are not enough.

steps.title: Create OAuth client credentials
steps.detail: Create a Web application client and add your redirect URIs.

steps.title: Run in Testing mode first
steps.detail: Only users on your test-user list can use the app, up to 100 test users. Refresh tokens for apps in testing expire after 7 days unless a Workspace admin marks the app as Trusted.

steps.title: Submit for verification
steps.detail: Verify your domain, publish your branding, then request a data access review in the Verification Center. Declare all your scopes, add up to three documentation links, and upload an unlisted YouTube demo video showing the consent flow, the app name and client ID on the consent screen, and how each sensitive and restricted scope is used. An agent can draft the scope justification and the video script.

blockers.title: Restricted scopes need a security assessment
blockers.detail: Google says storing or transmitting restricted scope data on servers requires a security assessment by an independent, Google-approved assessor using the CASA framework. It must be repeated at least every 12 months. The pages do not state the cost or how long the assessment takes.
blockers.what_to_do: Find out early whether your design triggers it. Because the rule covers transmitting data as well as storing it, an agent that reads mail through your servers will probably need it. Prefer a sensitive scope such as gmail.send if it covers your use case.

blockers.title: Testing mode and unverified app limits
blockers.detail: Testing apps are capped at 100 test users. A published but unverified app that requests sensitive or restricted scopes is capped at 100 total users, and users see warnings on the consent screen.
blockers.what_to_do: Use testing mode for development only. Plan for verification before launch.

blockers.title: Domain and policy requirements
blockers.detail: Your homepage must be on a verified domain you own, must describe what the app does and cannot be only a login page. The privacy policy should be on the same domain, linked from the homepage and from the consent screen, using the same link.
blockers.what_to_do: Set these up before submitting, not after the first rejection.
